# Design Review: Skill, Runbook, and Record Contract (RUN-STUDY Item 2)

**Design:** `.project/active/run-study-contract/design.md`
**Spec:** `.project/active/run-study-contract/spec.md` (Accepted)
**Concept-design:** `.project/concepts/run-study-skill-design.md` (Accepted — settled)
**Epic:** `.project/backlog/epic_run_study_capability.md` — Item 2
**Review File:** `.project/active/run-study-contract/design-review.md`
**Date:** 2026-08-19
**Reviewer posture:** fresh, skeptical; did not write the design

> **Note on process:** this session is non-interactive and operating under a standing
> directive not to spawn subagents. The product-lens was therefore run inline by the
> reviewer rather than by a `general-purpose` subagent, deriving the point independently
> from the concept, the prior concept, and the epic. The verdict block is at the end of
> this file and should be appended to `product-lens.md` by whoever carries this review back.

---

## The Point

Three owner pains and one structural gap drive this item.

- Quality regresses "if I don't phrase my prompt just the right way that got the executing agent to do what it did." (`run-study-skill.md`, via `spec.md:18`)
- There is no reproducibility floor, because no fixed list says what a study must record. (`spec.md:19`)
- When a finished study looks wrong, "I have no idea where to begin to improve the process for better outcomes." (`spec.md:20`)
- And the seam: "I prefer having sufficient structure in the artifacts from the executing study agent (e.g. context, goals, plan) so that another agent can effectively pick up the results and do the synthesis." (`spec.md:22`)

So: a prompt carrying only a goal and a scope must put an agent on the proof-of-life's
discipline, and the record that agent commits must let a second agent with **no execution
memory and no access outside the record directory** recover the framing per axis, the LCOE
result, every named constraint outcome, and every finding — each traced to a committed
artifact. A fact the second agent cannot recover is a defect in this contract, not in the
synthesis (`run-study-skill-design.md:61`).

This ladders into study-driven model development: a study that finds nothing pushing back
on an axis produces a model-development finding rather than a heatmap.

---

## Fundamental Assessment

**Sound, with one fired smell that is a hole in a rule rather than in the foundation.**

The central move — split the record into `snapshot.json` (resolved values, machine-checkable)
and `record.md` (arguments and judgments, human-readable), with fixed headings and an
explicit-nil rule — is the right piece of work and the simplest thing that discharges the
spec. It is Principle 1 ("obligations are formal; decisions are not") applied one level down,
and it earns its two conventions: fixed headings turn a missing fact into a missing heading,
and the explicit-nil rule collapses four would-be mechanisms into one. I could not describe a
simpler design that satisfies the fresh-administrator requirement. No premature abstraction,
no invented pattern where a repo convention exists (`.gitignore` negation, skill frontmatter),
no tooling built on speculation (the `record_lint.py` restraint at `design.md:279` is correct).

**Structural smell fired — ownership of an invariant moved without saying so.** The design
states the snapshot's completeness rule as "every fingerprint the manifest declares, by the
manifest's own name" (`design.md:231`). The manifest is the producer of that list; the record
is the consumer. The design gives the record no copy of the producer's declaration, so the
*only* party who can check the rule was followed — the administrator, who may read nothing
outside the record directory — cannot check it. The invariant silently becomes "the executor
remembered," which is exactly the discipline-in-the-prompt failure this epic exists to kill.
This escalates into the judgment, and it is **M2** below.

It does not condemn the approach. The fix is one added snapshot field, not a redesign, and
the same rule with that field is strictly better than a closed fingerprint triple. Verdict is
therefore APPROVE-WITH-FIXES, not Rework — recorded here explicitly so the call is visible
rather than buried.

The second design-level smell (a consumer compensating for a producer or platform guarantee)
did not fire: the record does not re-implement anything teax, the manifest, or the tools
guarantee. It snapshots them, which is the settled decision.

---

## Answers to the Five Briefed Questions

### 1. Do all 14 mandatory record items land in exactly one of the 17 sections?

**Yes — the mapping is clean, and I re-derived it independently.** Spec items 1–14
(`spec.md:72-85`) map to §3, §4, §2, §7, §8, §5, §9, §10, §12, §13, §14, §15, §16, §17
respectively. Nothing is dropped and nothing appears twice. The three sections carrying no
spec item are §1 (header), §6 (the framing-conditional per-axis account, which discharges
`spec.md:86`), and §11 (the window argument, split out of spec item 13). 17 − 3 = 14. The
table at `design.md:176-194` is accurate as an item-to-section map.

**But the map is only half the check, and the other half fails in two places.** Spec item 9
("the complete teax tuple of every store referenced") and spec item 13 (the whole snapshot
field list at `spec.md:87-98`) each have content the design routes to `snapshot.json`, while
the mapping table names a `record.md` section as their sole home. See **M1**.

### 2. Is the values/arguments split residue-free?

**No — one wrong home, one silent spec amendment, one unstated boundary.**

- **Glue: wrong home.** `design.md:235` routes "the glue's disclosure" to §17, the
  missing-evidence section. Glue is not missing evidence. It is *present* evidence about a
  model gap — values the harness supplied that the model did not (`run-study-skill-design.md:203`).
  §17 is mapped exclusively to spec item 14, so this also quietly doubles content into a
  section the map says is single-purpose. The spec already assigned this lesson a home:
  "Glue ledger disclosed with every study | **record snapshot field** | this item"
  (`spec.md:120`), which the design honors via `glue_ledger` (`design.md:221, 233`). The §17
  routing is an invention on top of a settled routing. See **M3**.
- **Window: a `[NEED]` amended without saying so.** `spec.md:95` puts "the window with its
  provenance ... **and how it was chosen**" inside the snapshot field list. The design moves
  "how it was chosen" to `record.md` §11 (`design.md:188, 235`) and keeps only
  `bounds`/`provenance` in the snapshot. I think the design's call is *right* — a rationale
  is an argument and belongs in prose — but it amends an owner-graded `[NEED]` and never says
  so in words. The mapping-table cell "snapshot's 'how it was chosen'" is the only trace, and
  a plan agent reading the spec's field list will put it back and create the exact drift B2
  exists to prevent. See **S1**.
- **Verification: residue-free, but the split's boundary is unstated.** Spec item 10's
  command, sampling scheme, and tolerance are resolved values, yet the design leaves all of
  §13 in `record.md` and puts nothing about verification in the snapshot. Nothing is doubled,
  so the invariant holds — but it shows the split is not the law `design.md:62-64` implies.
  Preflight results (§9) are the same class. The real rule is "the enumerated snapshot fields
  are the values; everything else lives in `record.md`," and saying that plainly stops the
  plan from migrating verification and preflight fields into `snapshot.json`. See **S2**.

### 3. Can a cold administrator execute the D2 snapshot rule?

**No.** The rule is "every fingerprint the manifest declares, by the manifest's own name"
(`design.md:231`). The administrator reads only the record directory (`design.md:128, 249`).
The snapshot's `manifest` block carries `digest` and `content_used` (`design.md:217`), and
`content_used` is scoped by `spec.md:90` to ties, objective catalog, baseline point and
headline, and oracle command — **not** the manifest's fingerprint declarations. So a cold
administrator sees a `fingerprints` map with some keys in it and has no way to tell whether
it is complete. Given Item 3's manifest carries at least three fingerprints
(indicator-input `[HARD]`, plus sealed `executable_fingerprint` and `semantic_fingerprint`
as provenance — `run-study-indicators/spec.md:40,42`) and the set is explicitly open, a
dropped fingerprint is both plausible and undetectable. This is the fired smell. See **M2**.

### 4. Does anything smuggle a judgment into an obligation, or a package name into a universal document?

**No judgment smuggled.** I read the runbook step list (`design.md:152`), the section list
(`design.md:176-194`), and the invariants (`design.md:241-251`) hunting for a preference among
axes, framings, routes, or results. Every obligation is "argue and record," never "prefer."
`design.md:247` states the rule and the design obeys it. The one wording that reads as a
judgment — "A cold administrator reads §1–§6 and knows the study" (`design.md:174`) — is a
claim about the section ordering, not an instruction to the executor, and does not ship.

**One package name at risk of shipping.** `design.md:66` gives the explicit-nil worked example
as "not applicable: `availability` is sensitivity-framed". `availability` is a stellarator
package input key. In the design it is illustrative; the template's own example at
`design.md:200` correctly uses `<axis>`. If the plan carries the `:66` phrasing into
`record-template.md` it violates the design's own zero-package-names invariant
(`design.md:246`). Cheap to prevent now. See **N1**.

### 5. Is D4 (one record, one directory) compatible with the concept-design's store rule?

**Compatible in principle, incomplete in structure.** D4 (`design.md:86`) says arms share one
record directory and one `record.md`, distinguished by a stable `arm-<slug>` used identically
in record subsections, snapshot store entries, and result filenames. The concept-design's rule
is one store per complete compatibility tuple, arms in one study definition sharing a store,
tuple differences meaning separate stores, comparison in the record and never in a merged
store (`run-study-skill-design.md:129`). D4 is exactly that shape, and the snapshot's
`arms[].store.compatibility_tuple` (`design.md:220`) carries the per-arm tuple. D3's rejection
of a fingerprint-tagged study id for the same reason is consistent.

**What is missing is how arms subdivide the seventeen fixed headings.** The concept-design
requires "one arm per section" (`run-study-skill-design.md:129`) and the epic requires LCOE and
qualified constraint outcomes **per arm** (`epic:412-413`). The design's fixed-headings
invariant (`design.md:244`) says a compliant record carries all seventeen headings verbatim, in
order — and says nothing about arm subheadings. So §3, §4, §6, §10, §12, and §13 have no stated
per-arm structure, and Item 6, the epic's decisive consumer, is the first thing to hit it. See
**M4**.

---

## Dimensional Review

### 1. Spec Compliance
**Assessment:** Concerns

The 14-item map is complete (Q1). The `[HARD]` items are honored: `.gitignore` one line after
line 23 — verified against the live file, where line 21 is `.claude/skills/*` and 22–23 are the
two existing negations (`design.md:92, 269`); the policy cited at its current path
(`design.md:270`); indicator vocabulary preserved exactly (`design.md:271`); records at
`exploration/<pkg>/studies/<study-id>/` with the proof-of-life untouched (`design.md:291`).

Two spec-routed obligations owned by **this item** are dropped from the runbook step list:

- **The pre-execution framing critique.** `spec.md:118` routes "Plan/framing critique before
  any point runs" to a runbook step depositing its verdict in the record's review outcomes, and
  `spec.md:82` makes it one of the named review outcomes. It survived a product-lens smell round
  specifically to get a record deposit (`product-lens.md:18, 25`). It does not appear in
  `design.md:152`. See **M5**.
- **Report-number traceability.** `spec.md:119` routes "Every report number traces to a
  committed artifact" to a runbook step (honesty lens). The design's list has a bare "report"
  step (`design.md:152`) and the obligation is nowhere stated. See **S3**.

**Capture-fidelity check.** The window `[NEED]` amendment (S1) is the one place the design
alters a spec-graded item without stating it. The `/show-me` `[REFERENT]` is carried correctly
and at the right scope (`design.md:203`) — it governs section weight, not the skill file, which
is the distinction `product-lens.md:14` fought for. The orchestrator rulings at `design.md:96-100`
are properly marked as supersessions with the superseded line cited, which is the right way to
do it.

One carried smell the design was handed and did not take up: `product-lens.md:26` said "Design
may sharpen the sensitivity-framing section to locate violations in the swept space." §6's
sensitivity counterpart still owes only the observed response plus a no-boundary-claim statement
(`design.md:203`). Declining is legitimate — it was CARRIED, not BLOCK — but it should be a
stated decline, not silence. See **N2**.

### 2. Pattern Consistency
**Assessment:** Pass

The design found and reused the repo's actual conventions rather than inventing: the
directory-form `.gitignore` negation with a working verification command (`design.md:269`), the
`browser-inspect/SKILL.md` frontmatter shape (`design.md:50, 138`), and the proof-of-life plan's
own three content forms as the source for the runbook's shape (`design.md:52`). The observation
that the proof-of-life already recorded review passes as named lenses with dispositions — so the
spec's `[NEED]` is a distillation, not an imposition — is the kind of grounding that makes a
design trustworthy. The ADR absence is handled the same way the concept-design handled it, with
no ids hand-minted (`design.md:30`).

### 3. Abstraction Quality
**Assessment:** Pass

Two abstractions, both earning their keep. Remove the values/arguments split and every fact is
either awkwardly narrated or buried in hashes. Remove the explicit-nil rule and you need four
bespoke mechanisms (framing-conditional sections, glue "none", the no-adapter case,
cross-fingerprint correlation) — the design says exactly this at `design.md:66` and it is right.
The four-line runbook micro-schema (`design.md:145-150`) is a formatting convention, not an
abstraction, which is the correct weight for the job. Nothing here would make me ask "why?"

### 4. Duplication Avoidance
**Assessment:** Concerns

The no-duplication invariant (`design.md:241`) is the design's central promise and it holds
everywhere except the two places M1 identifies, where a mapping-table cell and a heading name
content the snapshot owns. The rejected alternative "both, with the JSON normative and a prose
summary" (`design.md:84`) is rejected for the right reason. The one-way digest rule
(`design.md:126, 242`) is correct and the reason given — a two-way digest is uncomputable — is
the real one.

### 5. Data Structure Clarity
**Assessment:** Concerns

`snapshot.json`'s illustrative shape (`design.md:212-227`) is explicit and typed enough for a
plan to expand. Two gaps:

- **No `axis_groups` field.** The concept-design's snapshot explicitly copies in "declared axis
  groups with per-key provenance" (`run-study-skill-design.md:129`), and the design's own
  reasoning says resolved values belong in the snapshot. But the design puts axis groups in
  `record.md` §7 as prose, and `spec.md:87-98`'s field list omits them. The design is
  spec-conformant and concept-design-divergent, and does not say which it chose or why. See **S4**.
- **`study.entry_models` versus §7's axis groups.** These overlap in a way the design never
  disambiguates — a plan agent could reasonably read the per-key entry map as the axis-group
  declaration and write it twice. One sentence separating them prevents it. See **N3**.

The `glue_ledger_none: true` sibling (`design.md:233`) is a good, honest solution to a real JSON
ambiguity, and the reason given — an empty list and a forgotten field look identical — is exactly
right.

### 6. Route Safety
**Assessment:** Pass

Not a routing design in the HTTP sense; read as finding-routing and execution-route selection.
Both are explicit. The finding-routing home set is closed and named — {tool, runbook step, policy
rule, skill, modeling item, research round, documented seam} (`design.md:272`) — with no catch-all;
`unrouted` is a stated state that must be written, never a blank (`design.md:164`). Two execution
routes and no third, recorded with the reason (`design.md:152, 187`). No wildcard anywhere.

### 7. Bets & Decisions Integrity
**Assessment:** Concerns

B1–B4 are genuine claims about reality, each with a real "if false" consequence, and B2's "if
false" names the exact failure Principle 5 exists to prevent. The risks section then does
something rare and good: it names the window as the case most likely to falsify B2
(`design.md:281`) rather than asserting the bet holds. D1–D10 each name a rejected alternative
with the reason it lost; none is a mechanism choice dressed as inevitable. D6 is honest about
confirming the concept-design rather than deciding fresh (`design.md:88`).

**Hidden bet, unstated: the executor is reliable where nothing checks.** The design rests on it
in three places — the snapshot's fingerprint set is complete (M2), no template placeholder token
survives commit (`design.md:245`), and every heading is present and verbatim (`design.md:244`) —
and no party can verify any of the three from inside the record. B3 states the *reader-side* half
("a human reader can tell a missing section from a nil-discharged one") but not the *writer-side*
half, and the writer-side half is the one this epic exists because it failed before: discipline
that lived in one session's habits. The risks section calls the missing linter a risk
(`design.md:279`), which is the right restraint, but a risk is not a bet. Naming it as B5 changes
what Item 5 and Item 6 are watching for. See **S5**.

### 8. Reader Comprehension
**Assessment:** Pass

`design.md:62` states the core concept in one sentence before any mechanism, and the next
paragraph gives the reason in plain terms a tired engineer gets on one pass. The Core Concept →
Bets → Decisions → Architecture order builds the model in layers. The ASCII tree at
`design.md:108-124` is the fastest way into the artifact set and annotates each line with the
decision that produced it. Terms are anchored where introduced. I'd have understood this design
cold.

One count slip: D9 says "a reader cannot tell which of fifteen steps needs it" (`design.md:91`)
while the step list at `design.md:152` enumerates thirteen. Harmless to comprehension, but a plan
agent may treat "fifteen" as a target. See **N4**.

---

## Issues by Severity

### Critical — must fix (would produce a wrong or non-conformant implementation)

**M1. Two mapping-table rows name a `record.md` section as sole home for content the snapshot owns.**
*What's wrong:* §12's heading is "Compatibility tuples and cross-fingerprint correlation"
(`design.md:189`) and it is mapped to spec item 9, whose first clause — "the complete teax tuple
of every store referenced" (`spec.md:80`) — is a resolved value the design assigns to
`snapshot.json` at `arms[].store.compatibility_tuple` (`design.md:220`). §11 has the same problem:
its heading is "Study definition and window provenance" (`design.md:188`), and both the study
definition (`study.study_id`, `entry_models`, `strategy`) and the window's provenance are snapshot
fields (`design.md:218-219`). An implementer following the headings writes the tuples and the
provenance into `record.md`, which violates `design.md:241`.
*Smallest fix:* rename the two headings to name only what they carry — §11 "Window rationale — how
the window was chosen" and §12 "Cross-fingerprint correlation — what the boundary means" — and add
a mapping-table footnote that spec items 9 and 13 discharge across `snapshot.json` plus their
`record.md` argument section. The map stays 14-to-14; it stops lying about where the values live.

**M2. A cold administrator cannot check the D2 snapshot completeness rule.** *(fired smell)*
*What's wrong:* "every fingerprint the manifest declares, by the manifest's own name"
(`design.md:231`) is stated against a document the administrator may not read (`design.md:249`),
and `manifest.content_used` is scoped by `spec.md:90` to ties, objectives, baseline, and oracle
command — it carries no fingerprint declaration list. With Item 3's set open and already at three
(`run-study-indicators/spec.md:40,42`), a dropped fingerprint is undetectable from inside the record.
*Smallest fix:* require `manifest.content_used` to include the manifest's fingerprint declaration
block verbatim — names and values — and state the check the administrator runs: the key set of
`fingerprints` equals the key set of `manifest.content_used.fingerprints`. One field, and the rule
becomes executable by its only reader.

**M3. Glue disclosure is routed to the missing-evidence section.**
*What's wrong:* `design.md:235` sends "the glue's disclosure" to §17, "What this record does not
contain." Glue is present evidence of a model gap — values the harness supplied that the model did
not (`run-study-skill-design.md:203`) — not absent evidence. It also puts a second kind of content
into a section the mapping table gives solely to spec item 14, and it overrides the spec's own
routing of this lesson to the snapshot field (`spec.md:120`).
*Smallest fix:* delete "the glue's disclosure in §17" from `design.md:235`. The `glue_ledger` field
plus its explicit nil (`design.md:233`) discharges the obligation. If a prose reading is wanted,
its home is §8, where the model-underdevelopment statements already live — same kind of claim,
already-mandatory section.

**M4. The per-arm structure of the seventeen sections is undefined.**
*What's wrong:* D4 says arms are "distinguished by a stable `arm-<slug>` id used identically in
record subsections" (`design.md:86`) but no section is stated to have arm subsections, and the
fixed-headings invariant (`design.md:244`) mentions only the seventeen. The concept-design requires
"one arm per section" (`run-study-skill-design.md:129`) and the epic requires LCOE and constraint
outcomes per arm (`epic:412-413`). Item 6 — the epic's decisive proof — is the first consumer.
*Smallest fix:* add one rule to the Record Section Order: "A section whose content is arm-scoped
(§3, §4, §6, §10, §12, §13) subdivides into `#### arm-<slug>` subsections, one per arm, using the
same ids as `snapshot.json`'s `arms[]`. A single-arm study states one subsection or omits the level
entirely." Then extend the fixed-headings invariant to say arm subheadings are additive and do not
break heading conformance.

**M5. The pre-execution framing critique is dropped from the runbook step list.**
*What's wrong:* `spec.md:118` routes it to a runbook step depositing its verdict in the record's
review outcomes, and `spec.md:82` makes it one of the named review outcomes. It is owned by *this
item*, and it survived a product-lens round precisely to acquire a record deposit
(`product-lens.md:18, 25`). It is absent from `design.md:152`.
*Smallest fix:* insert it into the step list between the framing-argument step and preflight:
"framing critique before any point runs → **Deposits:** record.md § Review outcomes."

**M6. The design contradicts itself on who writes the discovery log.** *(found in the general sweep, not in the five briefed questions)*
*What's wrong:* `design.md:128` states "The discovery log is written by both — a row per finding, at
the moment the finding is filed." `design.md:249` states the invariant "the administrator writes
nothing else [but `synthesis.md`] and reads nothing outside the record directory." `DISCOVERY_LOG.md`
lives at `exploration/<pkg>/studies/DISCOVERY_LOG.md` — outside the record directory — and appending a
row to a markdown table requires reading the file. The concept-design settles the administrator's
scope the strict way twice (`run-study-skill-design.md:107, 165`). The runbook's administer sequence
compounds it by ending with "file any record-contract gap as a process finding" (`design.md:152`).
This is not a wording slip: it decides whether administer mode can be run by a genuinely sandboxed
fresh session, which is the epic's decisive proof (`epic:401`).
*Smallest fix:* keep the invariant and route the administrator's findings through the record. The
administrator states every gap in `synthesis.md` § "What the record does not support" — which
`design.md:168` already makes mandatory — and the discovery-log row is filed by whoever carries the
synthesis back, outside administer mode. Then change `design.md:128` to "The discovery log is written
by the executor; the administrator's findings reach it via `synthesis.md`." If instead the owner wants
the administrator to append rows directly, the invariant at `:249` must be amended in words to
"reads no study evidence outside the record directory; may append to the discovery log" — but that
weakens the sandbox the fresh-administrator check depends on, and it should be an explicit owner call,
not an inconsistency.

### Major — should fix

**S1. State the window `[NEED]` amendment in words.** `spec.md:95` puts "how it was chosen" in the
snapshot; the design moves it to §11 (`design.md:188, 235`) with only a mapping-table cell as
evidence. The call is right; the silence is the problem — a plan agent reading the spec's field list
will restore it and create the drift B2 warns about. Add one line to D2: "The window's bounds and
provenance are snapshot values; 'how it was chosen' is an argument and moves to §11, amending
`spec.md:95`."

**S2. State the split's actual boundary.** Verification (spec item 10) and preflight (spec item 7)
carry resolved values — command, sampling scheme, tolerance, per-gate pass/fail — and live wholly in
`record.md`. Nothing is doubled, but `design.md:62-64` reads as a universal law it is not. Add to
Required Invariants: "The enumerated `snapshot.json` fields are the value side; every other required
fact lives in `record.md`, including the resolved values inside §9 and §13." This stops a plan agent
from migrating them.

**S3. The report step must name its obligation.** `spec.md:119` routes "every report number traces to
a committed artifact" to a runbook step (honesty lens), owned by this item. `design.md:152` has a bare
"report". Give the step its `**Fails closed when:**` or deposit line so the obligation survives into
the runbook text.

**S4. Say where declared axis groups live and why.** `run-study-skill-design.md:129` names them as
snapshot content; `spec.md:87-98`'s field list omits them; the design puts them in `record.md` §7 and
does not mention the divergence. Under Principle 5 this is exactly the "recorded in two homes drifts"
case waiting to happen. One line in D2 or the mapping table: axis groups are record-side because
per-key provenance is a declaration the executor argues for, not a resolved digest — and the snapshot
therefore carries no `axis_groups` field, deliberately.

**S5. Name the unstated bet.** The design rests on executor reliability where nothing checks — the
fingerprint set (M2), unreplaced tokens (`design.md:245`), heading conformance (`design.md:244`) — and
B3 states only the reader-side half. Add **B5: "A stated, unenforced contract is enough to hold record
structure across studies before any linter exists. *If false → records drift silently, and the epic
has rebuilt discipline-in-the-prompt one layer down.*"** The missing linter is already a risk
(`design.md:279`); the bet is what makes Items 5 and 6 the evidence for it.

### Minor — consider

thirteen. Fix the number or drop it.

## Recommendations

1. **Fix M1–M5 before the plan stage.** All five are local edits to `design.md` — two headings, one
   snapshot field, one arm-subsection rule, one runbook step. None touches the architecture.
2. **Take M2 first.** It is the fired smell and the one finding that changes what the record *is*: a
   contract whose central rule its only reader can check, versus one that trusts the writer.
3. **Fold S1, S2, and S4 into D2.** All three are the same category — the values/arguments boundary
   stated precisely enough that a plan agent cannot re-double a fact. D2 is where a plan agent will
   look.
4. **Keep the de-risk order as written.** The skeleton dry run against the proof-of-life
   (`design.md:324`) is the right first move and will exercise M1, M2, and S2 on real facts before
   any document is finished.
5. **Do not build the linter.** The restraint at `design.md:279` is correct. B5 (S5) makes the bet
   visible so Items 5 and 6 produce evidence for or against it; that is the right time to decide.

## Product-Lens Verdict Block

```
## design — 2026-08-19 — rev Item 2 design draft (`.project/active/run-study-contract/design.md`)

Point (re-derived): A study run from a goal-and-scope-only prompt must reach the proof-of-life
floor, and its committed record must let a fresh administrator — no execution memory, no access
outside the record directory — recover framing per axis, LCOE, every named constraint outcome,
and every finding traced to a committed artifact; every lesson lands in exactly one home.
[source: `.project/concepts/run-study-skill.md` (Owner's Words, SC-1/SC-3);
`.project/concepts/run-study-skill-design.md` (Principles 1/3/5, Core Model, Required Invariants);
`.project/concepts/study-driven-model-development.md` (LCOE + constraint focus, discovery log);
`.project/backlog/epic_run_study_capability.md` Item 2 and Item 6 criteria, grade: owner]

Falsifier: A record can satisfy every structural rule in this design and still leave the fresh
administrator unable to confirm the snapshot's fingerprint set is complete, unable to find LCOE
and constraint outcomes per arm in an A/B study, and unable to file the contract gap it found.

Findings:
- `design-F1` [DO] The snapshot's completeness rule ("every fingerprint the manifest declares")
  is stated against a document the administrator may not read, and the record carries no copy of
  the manifest's fingerprint declarations. The rule's only reader cannot execute it.
  — `.project/concepts/run-study-skill-design.md:61,165` (owner-accepted design) — disposition: BLOCK
- `design-F2` [DO] The seventeen fixed headings define no per-arm structure, while the accepted
  design requires one arm per section and the epic requires LCOE and constraint outcomes per arm.
  — `.project/concepts/run-study-skill-design.md:129`; `epic:412-413` (owner) — disposition: BLOCK
- `design-F3` [DO] The administrator is required to write discovery-log rows (`design.md:128`)
  while the same design forbids the administrator from writing anything but `synthesis.md` and
  reading anything outside the record directory (`design.md:249`). The improvement loop's entry
  point for a cold reader is self-contradictory.
  — `.project/concepts/run-study-skill-design.md:107,165` (owner-accepted design) — disposition: BLOCK
- `design-F4` [DON'T] Glue disclosure routed to the missing-evidence section; glue is present
  evidence of a model gap and the spec already routed it to the snapshot field.
  — `.project/active/run-study-contract/spec.md:120` (owner-graded routing) — disposition: NOTE

Smells:
- Ownership of an invariant moved without saying so: "the snapshot's fingerprint set is complete"
  passes from the manifest (producer) to the executor's discipline (`design.md:231`), with no
  party able to verify it. FIRED — escalated into the Fundamental Assessment; one-field fix, so
  it does not condemn the approach.
- Consumer compensating for a producer or platform guarantee: did not fire. The record snapshots
  teax, manifest, and tool facts rather than re-deriving them, which is the settled decision.

Gate: BLOCKED (`design-F1`, `design-F2`, `design-F3`) — all three resolvable by local edits to
`design.md`; no architectural change implied.

## Additional Must-Fix Found in Sweep

**M6. The design contradicts itself on who writes the discovery log.**
*What's wrong:* `design.md:128` states "The discovery log is written by both — a row per finding, at
the moment the finding is filed." `design.md:249` states the invariant "the administrator writes
nothing else [but `synthesis.md`] and reads nothing outside the record directory." `DISCOVERY_LOG.md`
lives at `exploration/<pkg>/studies/DISCOVERY_LOG.md` — outside the record directory — and appending a
row to a markdown table requires reading the file. The concept-design settles the administrator's
scope the strict way twice (`run-study-skill-design.md:107, 165`). The runbook's administer sequence
compounds it by ending with "file any record-contract gap as a process finding" (`design.md:152`).
This is not a wording slip: it decides whether administer mode can be run by a genuinely sandboxed
fresh session, which is the epic's decisive proof (`epic:401`).
*Smallest fix:* keep the invariant and route the administrator's findings through the record. The
administrator states every gap in `synthesis.md` § "What the record does not support" — which
`design.md:168` already makes mandatory — and the discovery-log row is filed by whoever carries the
synthesis back, outside administer mode. Then change `design.md:128` to "The discovery log is written
by the executor; the administrator's findings reach it via `synthesis.md`." If instead the owner wants
the administrator to append rows directly, the invariant at `:249` must be amended in words to
"reads no study evidence outside the record directory; may append to the discovery log" — but that
weakens the sandbox the fresh-administrator check depends on, and it should be an explicit owner call,
not an inconsistency.

*(Numbered M6 and placed here because it surfaced in the general sweep rather than in the five briefed
questions; it belongs with M1–M5 in severity and is carried in the verdict below as `design-F3`.)*

---

**Overall:** Revise — **APPROVE-WITH-FIXES**

The design is the right piece of work, the core split is right, and the complexity matches the
problem. Six local edits stand between it and a plan that would implement it correctly:

1. **M1** — rename §11 and §12 to name only what they carry; footnote the split discharge of spec items 9 and 13.
2. **M2** — add the manifest's fingerprint declaration block to `manifest.content_used`, and state the administrator's completeness check.
3. **M3** — delete the §17 glue routing; the `glue_ledger` field plus explicit nil discharges it.
4. **M4** — state the `#### arm-<slug>` subsection rule for the six arm-scoped sections, and that arm subheadings do not break heading conformance.
5. **M5** — add the pre-execution framing critique to the runbook step list, depositing into §14.
6. **M6** — resolve the discovery-log contradiction; keep the administrator sandbox and route gaps through `synthesis.md`.

Then S1–S5 (five sentences, mostly into D2) and N1–N4 (four one-liners). None requires rework of the
architecture, the section set, or the two governing conventions.

**Next Steps:** Record resolutions above, then re-run `/_my_design` (or return to the design-agent
session) and point it at this review to incorporate. The reviewer does not edit the design. After the
six must-fixes land, this is ready for `/_my_plan`; the de-risk step (skeleton dry run against the
proof-of-life) should be the plan's first phase, as `design.md:324` proposes.

Review written. Summary of what it found.

**Fundamental assessment: sound.** The values/arguments split (`snapshot.json` for resolved values, `record.md` for arguments) plus fixed headings plus the explicit-nil rule is the right shape and the simplest thing that discharges the spec. I could not describe a simpler design that satisfies the fresh-administrator requirement. No premature abstraction, and the restraint on not building a linter is correct.

**One structural smell fired** — ownership of an invariant moved without saying so — and it is M2 below. I recorded it as escalated but did not force Rework, since the fix is one snapshot field, not a redesign. That call is stated visibly in the review rather than buried.

**Six must-fixes:**

1. **M1** — §11 and §12 headings ("Study definition and window provenance", "Compatibility tuples…") name content the snapshot owns (`design.md:188-189` vs `:218-220`). An implementer following the headings doubles the fact and breaks the design's own no-duplication invariant.
2. **M2** — a cold administrator **cannot** execute the D2 snapshot rule. "Every fingerprint the manifest declares" is stated against a document they may not read, and `manifest.content_used` is scoped by `spec.md:90` to ties/objectives/baseline/oracle — no fingerprint list. Fix: copy the manifest's fingerprint declaration block into the snapshot.
3. **M3** — glue disclosure routed to §17, the missing-evidence section (`design.md:235`). Glue is *present* evidence of a model gap, and `spec.md:120` already routed it to the snapshot field.
4. **M4** — the seventeen headings define no per-arm structure, while the concept-design requires one arm per section and the epic requires LCOE and constraint outcomes per arm. Item 6 hits this first.
5. **M5** — the pre-execution framing critique is dropped from the runbook step list, despite `spec.md:118` routing it here and a product-lens round having fought to give it a record deposit.
6. **M6** (found in the sweep) — the design contradicts itself on who writes the discovery log: `:128` says both roles, `:249` says the administrator writes only `synthesis.md` and reads nothing outside the record directory. This decides whether administer mode can run genuinely sandboxed.

**On the briefed questions:** the 14-item map is clean and I re-derived it (14 items → 14 sections, three sections carry no spec item: header, framing rule, window argument). The values/arguments split is *not* residue-free — glue (M3), the window's "how it was chosen" silently amending `spec.md:95` (S1), and an unstated boundary where verification and preflight values sit in `record.md` (S2). No judgment is smuggled into any obligation; one package name (`availability`, `design.md:66`) is at risk of shipping into the template. D4 is compatible with the store rule in principle, incomplete in structure (M4).

Plus five should-fixes — including naming the unstated bet that the executor is reliable where nothing checks — and four minors.

**Verdict: APPROVE-WITH-FIXES.** None of the fixes touches the architecture, the section set, or the two governing conventions.
